summary: Register describes a steel tower with its address at Tweed, Ontario; a map note says it is missing from the 4th-edition Pembroke sheet 31F.

events.note: Register map note: the tower appears on the 3rd (1977) edition of Pembroke topographic map 31F.

evidence.supports: Register describes the tower as steel; map note on 4th and 3rd editions of Pembroke sheet 31F
evidence.quote: Steel. No longer appears on Pembroke topographic map 31F (4th ed.) however, it does appear on the 3rd (1977) edition

evidence.supports: Register address is Tweed, ON, Canada
Most Ontario towers were erected between the 1920s and the 1950s
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: Towers were under Lands and Forests, which became the MNR in 1972
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: Lookouts were used less through the 1960s as aerial spotting and fire-fighting crews took over
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

sources.title: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts: Preserving Their History

notes_for_editor: The only tower-specific source is the firelookout.ca record: a steel tower, an address of Tweed, ON, the coordinates, and a map note. Its height, year built and tower type fields are N/A. The Canada Lookouts Ontario index lists Lyndoch with no details. A firelookout.ca record for Jamieson's Mountain Fire Tower names Lyndoch and Raglan townships in its address, but its coordinates (45.25343, -77.24133) are about 13 km from this tower, so it is not used. Nothing in the sources links this tower to the Tweed Forest Fire District. No build date, status or staffing was found.
